subject: Has anyone ever productionized a Stan model on Azure Machine Learning?

messages.author: a997b66afa263bd1
messages.subject: Has anyone ever productionized a Stan model on Azure Machine Learning?
parts:
Has anyone ever productionized a Stan model on Azure Machine Learning? We are using a STAN model to predict housing prices , and would like to expose the results as a webservice. The Microsoft Azure Machine Learning module has a feature to automatically generate anAPI from the resultant dataset of a R script and we plan to use this. However even small scripts are taking a lot of time to run -so I cant even think what will happen when I run the STAn code which takes 2 days to train the data. If anyone has done thi before I will be grateful for some suggestions

Thanks and Regards
Upasana

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Has anyone ever productionized a Stan model on Azure Machine Learning?
parts:
No idea what Azure is --- we haven't had an easy time
with all things Windows, though, given its quirky behavior
for C++.

You might try either a subset of data or use something like
variational inference if you can deal with an approximate answer
(which is what "machine learning" approaches usually do, though
often with even simpler penalized max likelihood and plug-in of
the point inferences).

- Bob

messages.author: 4d367efe02bee69e
messages.subject: Re: Has anyone ever productionized a Stan model on Azure Machine Learning?
parts:
Hi,
No, as far as I know, and I talked to some Azure ML developers, it is not possible now. The problem is that a VM that hosts AML has to have Rtools preinstalled, which is not the case, and Rtools cannot be installed like a normal package. Perhaps make a feature suggestion. I will also try from my side.

Regards,
Slawek

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Has anyone ever productionized a Stan model on Azure Machine Learning?

Yes, we still need a C++ compiler, so even CmdStan recommends Rtools because
we keep Stan compatible with it. But other C++ toolchains can work --- we just
need a relatively recent C++ compiler and make.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Has anyone ever productionized a Stan model on Azure Machine Learning?
parts:
On Tuesday, August 25, 2015 at 7:58:17 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:

We haven't tried a Windows compiler in a long time, but at v1.0 (3 years ago), Stan had been compatible with MSVC.

It doesn't need make if you can figure out the builds. If you're using g++ or clang++, it should be straightforward with make.

It is not quite that bleak. In 2014, someone actually had MSVC somewhat working:

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/A_WcImpwaYA/rePu_Tc-ICQJ

IIRC, there may have been some problem with the Boost we were using at the time being too old, which should have resolved itself once we upgraded to Boost 1.58.0.

Ben

messages.author: a997b66afa263bd1
messages.subject: Re: Has anyone ever productionized a Stan model on Azure Machine Learning?
parts: To let everyone know, STAN runs on Azure Machine Learning just fine. I have not 'trained' a model yet, but I am using STAN in 'Fixed Param' mode to predict on 'test' data using parameters retrieved from the trining model on my local computer. I don't know if there will be any issues to run a training , but so far it seems stan performs exactly same as it does in my local PC
